svg.title: Johan S. Varughese. I study when machine learning can be trusted.

text.tspan: Abstract.
A model can be accurate and still not deserve trust. I work on where that
trust breaks, across six areas of machine learning: privacy in federated learning,
robustness to poisoned clients, the integrity of training runs, bias in LLM-as-judge
evaluation, interpretability under activation steering, and mode-seeking variational
inference.
Each project ends the same way, with a method and an honest account of
where it fails. I then take those methods where failure has a cost: ECG arrhythmia
detection, HER2 breast-cancer pathology and district election operations.
I’m a final-year B.Tech student in CSE (AI) at Mar Baselios College of Engineering
and Technology, where I founded IRIS, the college’s first undergraduate research
lab.
Seven manuscripts so far, six of them to be submitted.
